findings.title: PIE mouse drawing is dead: Enhanced Input binds capture null actions (SetupInputComponent runs before BeginPlay)
findings.evidence: SetupInputComponent() { ... EIC->BindAction(DrawStartAction, ETriggerEvent::Started, ...) } // DrawStartAction created later in BeginPlay()
findings.detail: APlayerController::SetPlayer -> InitInputSystem -> SetupInputComponent runs before BeginPlay (UE 5.8 PlayerController.cpp:765,5376); the runtime-created UInputActions exist only after BeginPlay, so both binds capture nullptr. UEnhancedInputComponent::BindAction stores the pointer with no null check (EnhancedInputComponent.h:482) and a null-action binding can never match, so LMB never reaches BeginDraw/EndDraw. The recorded PIE evidence drove drawing through the MCP bridge, masking this.
findings.recommended_fix: Create the UInputAction/UInputMappingContext objects in the controller constructor (or bind inside BeginPlay after creating them), keeping one legality path; add an automation test that synthesizes the action trigger headlessly.

findings.title: StateHash fails open: states serializing above the fixed 4096-byte buffer silently hash to the FNV offset basis
findings.evidence: std::vector<uint8_t> Buffer(4096); const size_t N = SerializeState(State, Buffer.data(), Buffer.size()); return Fnv1a64(Buffer.data(), N); // SerializeState returns 0 when Buf.size() > OutCapacity
findings.detail: Any future state over 4096 bytes (topology/flow growth in later slices) collapses to the empty hash, silently false-greening replay-equality. Not reachable at slice-1 scale, but the failure mode is silent and touches the ODN-9/11 contract.
findings.recommended_fix: Grow the buffer adaptively (retry with doubled capacity when SerializeState returns 0) or assert/return a distinct error hash; add a >4096-byte state test.

findings.title: StepScenario silently drops replay commands beyond 16 per tick - live/replay diverge with no ReplayError latch
findings.evidence: FCommand Cmds[16]; int32_t N = 0; for (const FLoggedCommand &E : State.ActionLog) { if (E.ApplyTick == Tick && N < 16) { Cmds[N++] = E.Cmd; } }
findings.detail: ApplyEdit logs every live edit with apply_tick = Tick+1, so 17 edits between two steps share one tick; the 17th is dropped silently, so replay under-applies the log while the live path applied everything - exactly the divergence the latch exists to catch.
findings.recommended_fix: Latch ReplayError (or at minimum count and report) when a tick's log entries exceed the cap; make the cap a named constant with a test at the boundary.

findings.title: EqualCostHops indexes the stale table's arrays with current-topology slots - out-of-bounds read when the topology grew after the table was built
findings.evidence: if (R.N == 0 || R.HopOffset.size() != R.N*R.N) return false; NodeSlot(T, FromNode, Fs); const uint64_t Idx = Fs * R.N + Ds; OutOffset = R.HopOffset[Idx];
findings.detail: The shape guard checks only the table vs itself; Fs/Ds come from the CURRENT topology. If T grew since the rebuild, Fs can exceed R.N and HopOffset[Idx] reads out of bounds. No in-repo caller hits the window today (Step rebuilds on Gen change before the flow runs), but the API takes (R, T) as a pair and invites mismatched use.
findings.recommended_fix: Guard R.N == T.NodeAlive.size() (or carry the topology Gen in the table and check it) and return false on mismatch.

findings.title: Step is unguarded at the same tick: re-entry double-applies commands, double-spawns demand and redraws the nonce
findings.evidence: if (Tick < State.Tick) { State.ReplayError = true; return; } // no guard for Tick == State.Tick
findings.detail: Backward ticks latch, but an equal tick silently re-applies that tick's commands (duplicating pipes), re-spawns tick-matched demand and moves the RNG. The shipped driver/scenario callers never do this, but the spine's caller-divergence protection is asymmetric.
findings.recommended_fix: Latch ReplayError (or no-op) when Tick == State.Tick, mirroring the backward guard.

findings.title: ApplyEdit (the live edit fast-path used by every player draw) has zero automated coverage
findings.evidence: grep -rln ApplyEdit tests/ Source/PacketPlumberCoreTests/ -> no matches
findings.detail: The live path is the production entry point (EndDraw -> DrawPipe -> ApplyEdit) and carries the E10 live/replay-equality burden; only the replay path (Step with commands) is tested. A divergence here is exactly what the contract forbids.
findings.recommended_fix: Add spine-check + automation tests driving ApplyEdit (valid draw, each rejection, then replay-equality vs a Step-replayed run of the same log).

findings.title: Routing tier-cost steering (capacity-cost ladder, user ruling 2026-08-13) untested - all routing tests use uniform TIER_STANDARD
findings.evidence: CHECK(PP::EqualCostHops(Rt4, T4, S4, DK, Off, Cnt) && Cnt == 2, "equal-cost ECMP set must have two hops"); // diamond legs all standard
findings.detail: The Dijkstra prices edges by tier cost (20/10/5) so flows prefer fat pipes; no test pins that a shorter-narrow path loses to a longer-wide one. This is ruling-carrying behavior with zero direct coverage.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a two-path topology with different tiers asserting the cheaper-cost (fatter) path is chosen.

findings.title: Failed replayed command -> ReplayError latch has no test (only the backward-tick trigger is covered)
findings.evidence: CHECK(S.ReplayError == true, "backward tick must latch ReplayError (never silent)");
findings.detail: PP_Sim.h:78 latches ReplayError when a replayed command fails ApplyDraw validation - the ODN-2 'never silent' guarantee for replay divergence. That branch is never exercised.
findings.recommended_fix: Feed Step a log containing an invalid command (e.g. self-loop) and assert the latch.

findings.title: E29 recovery only partially covered: drop-back asserted, but re-route and redelivery after severance never tested
findings.evidence: CHECK(S2.Flow.Packets.size() == 1, "the packet must survive the severance");
findings.detail: The E29 promise is automatic migration at the next junction; the test stops at drop-back and never proves the packet re-forwards on the rebuilt table and delivers.
findings.recommended_fix: Extend the E29 test: sever, redraw an alternate path, step, assert delivery.

findings.title: Multi-packet bundle capacity contention in the serve pass has no coverage
findings.evidence: CHECK(Bu2.N == 1 && Bu2.BundleCap[0] == 55, "mixed-tier bundle cap must sum member capacities (15+40)");
findings.detail: The serve pass is FIFO with min(need, remaining) sharing - the pre-QoS contention behavior. Only cap sums are tested; two packets sharing one bundle is untested.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a two-packet one-bundle test asserting deterministic FIFO service and total served <= capacity.

findings.title: Camera-fit mapping duplicated between the view and the command bus with different size sources, and never re-fit after the first layout
findings.evidence: view: GetCachedGeometry().GetLocalSize() ... FitScale = FMath::Min(...); bus: PC->GetViewportSize(VW, VH) ... Scale = FMath::Min(ViewportSize.X / WorldW, ...)
findings.detail: The same fit exists as two independent copies fed by widget-space vs viewport-space sizes (diverges under DPI scale or if the widget ever stops filling the viewport). Additionally the comment claims 'NativeTick re-fits once the real size lands' but NativeTick never recomputes FitScale/FitOffset - the fit is computed once at BindRun from possibly-zero geometry with a 1280x720 fallback.
findings.recommended_fix: Extract one shared fit function; recompute in NativeTick when the local size changes; keep both callers on the same size source.

findings.title: Road ribbons rotate about the widget origin (default pivot 0,0), not their center - any non-horizontal road renders displaced
findings.evidence: CasingSlot->SetPosition(Center - FVector2D((Width + 4.0f) * 0.5f, ...)); FWidgetTransform CasingT; CasingT.Angle = Angle; CasingBorder->SetRenderTransform(CasingT); // no SetRenderTransformPivot
findings.detail: The slot is positioned for the unrotated rect, then rotated about its top-left. Horizontal demo roads are unaffected; a diagonal draw (any node pair not sharing a row) displaces the ribbon off the node pair. Story 1.2's ribbon-road claim is only proven horizontal.
findings.recommended_fix: Call SetRenderTransformPivot(FVector2D(0.5f, 0.5f)) on both borders (or bake the rotation into the slot layout).

findings.title: Snap quantizes the cursor to its tile cell before the radius test - the E4 'world px, inclusive' snap is effectively tile-granular
findings.evidence: const int32 TileX = static_cast<int32>(FMath::FloorToDouble((ScreenPos.X - OffsetX) / (Scale * PP::kTilePx))); ... const int64_t D2 = PP::Dist2(Pos, GridPos);
findings.detail: ScreenToGrid floors away up to a full tile (26 px) of sub-tile precision before Dist2 runs, so clicks within the 36 px radius can miss and clicks beyond it can hit. The E4 contract (compare in world px) is not faithfully implemented.
findings.recommended_fix: Keep the cursor in world-px space for the snap distance test (compare px distances, not tile-corner distances); quantize only for placement.

findings.title: PIE fixture and demand are hand-copied into StartRun instead of sharing PP_Scenario's builder, contradicting the PR's 'SHARED code' (UAD-17) claim
findings.evidence: PP::SpawnNode(SimState.Topology, PP::FNodeKind::Terminal, 2, 2);  // SCENARIO_SOURCE ... for (uint64_t T = 10; T <= 100000; T += 10) { PP::FlowSeedDemand(...); }
findings.detail: The positions match PP_Scenario.h's constants but as literals with comments; the demand plan is a different hand-rolled plan (every 10 ticks to 100000 vs the scenario's 5..95+98). Decision #6 in the PR body claims every surface builds from the shared builder - the PIE surface does not, so PIE-vs-golden parity is by copy-paste, not construction.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a BuildRunFixture-style entry to PP_Scenario.h (fixture + run demand) and call it from StartRun.

findings.title: The headline inter-snapshot easing is vacuous (From == To always); actual motion is a fixed 0.5 exponential smoother, and bHasPrev is never restored after a topology change
findings.evidence: const FVector2D FromGrid = bHasPrev ? PacketPosIn(PrevSnapshot, Packet) : PacketPosIn(CurSnapshot, Packet); const FVector2D ToGrid = PacketPosIn(CurSnapshot, Packet); ... const FVector2D Smooth = FMath::Lerp(Prev, Target, 0.5f);
findings.detail: PacketPosIn derives position from the CURRENT packet's FromNode/ToNode/Progress against a snapshot's node table - node tables are static, so FromGrid == ToGrid and Lerp(From,To,Eased) is a no-op; the EaseInOut 'across BOTH fractions' claim in the PR body/comments does not describe the code. bHasPrev going false at the first topology change changes nothing visible precisely because the path was already dead. The visible motion is the 0.5 temporal lerp - smooth, but not the documented mechanic.
findings.recommended_fix: Carry each packet's prev-position (per-snapshot packet entries) so From differs from To, or document the actual smoothing honestly; restore/reset bHasPrev deliberately.
